about: Research pass on the SGit CLI site (sgit.ai: docs on architecture, the two-branch model, security and crypto, credentials and read keys, append lanes, partial clones, limits, the vault catalogue and four policy vaults), sharness.ai (Process Behaviour Policies, the PBP on one page, the levels, the decision engine and the landscape; the existing sharness2-* animation captures were not repeated), ruv.sgit.ai (home page) and two newsroom.sgit.ai pages for the public vault survey. 28 captures, 21 cropped regions each inspected by eye. Gaps: no article pages captured; the vault apps themselves were not opened or cloned; sharness.ai /code/browser and the playground were left to the sharness2-* series; ruv.sgit.ai sub-pages (shop, ledger, POCs) not captured; the try page terminal and the sgit-maps embed were not exercised; vault pages other than Hope or enforcement, Agent Desk, Licence to Operate and Kit Bag are described from the catalogue only.
cautions: Every sgit.ai vault page and newsroom.sgit.ai/llms.txt print read keys in full in the page text; the captures under captures/wsgit-* therefore contain read keys in page.html, page.txt and llms.txt. They are published on purpose by their owners, but this JSON and the PNG crops carry none; do not republish the raw captures.
The home page "What the server sees" diagram shows illustrative object and ref ids in hex; its crop was discarded under the no-key-like-strings rule. Use the /security/ table crop instead.
Agent Desk app screenshots carry small contact text in the app sidebar; no crop saved. ruv.sgit.ai's five-steps section ends with a contact email address; the crop stops above it.

sharness.ai /design/policies/ prompt-injection table quotes example injected commands as the site's own illustrations; the crop shows them, the JSON does not quote them. sgit.ai/llms.txt carries "Notes for agents" and newsroom.sgit.ai/llms.txt carries instructions addressed to reviewer agents; recorded as material, not followed.

sgit.ai pages show site v0.7.87 dated 13 Oct 2026 while the capture is 29 Oct 2026; the site footer says thirty vaults while the catalogue says fifty-four. Figures may be stale relative to the CLI (llms.txt mentions sgit-ai 0.21.0; sharness.ai mentions 0.24.x).
Hope or enforcement and Agent Desk numbers are deterministic simulations with labelled assumptions, not measurements of a model; say "simulated" on any slide.
All claims are own-site (A2 at most). The partial-clone timings are the CLI team's single-environment numbers.
The limitations page says commit author attribution is not yet recorded; other pages mention signatures in later CLI versions. Not reconciled.

claims.text: sgit encrypts files client-side with AES-256-GCM before they leave the machine, and the server stores ciphertext under opaque ids.

evidence.quote: Clone, commit, branch, diff and merge folders of files that are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before they leave your machine. The server stores ciphertext under opaque IDs, it never sees your filenames, your contents, or your commit messages.

claims.text: A commit snapshots the folder into a git-like object graph of commits, trees and blobs, each object encrypted client-side and content-addressed, so only changed ciphertext is pushed.

evidence.quote: When you commit, sgit snapshots the folder into a git-like object graph, commits pointing at trees pointing at content blobs, and encrypts every object client-side. When you push, only changed ciphertext travels.

claims.text: The vault key is three things in one string: the vault's address on the server, the credential, and the root of the key hierarchy.

evidence.quote: is three things in one string: the address of the vault on the server, the credential to access it, and the root of the local key-derivation hierarchy.

claims.text: sgit differs from git in three deliberate ways: no staging area, the key is URL, auth and encryption key in one, and two layers of branches.
sgit supports init, clone, status, commit, push, pull, fetch, branches, three-way merge, history, revert, reset and stash, but not rebase, cherry-pick, bisect, blame, hooks, submodules or tags.

evidence.quote:
No for: pull requests (a hosting-platform
  construct layered on merge, not a git primitive), a staging area or partial commits
  (a commit snapshots the whole folder), bisect, blame, rebase, cherry-pick, hooks,
  submodules and tags.

claims.text: Each clone works on a private clone branch whose key never leaves the machine, so two agents on one vault cannot overwrite each other's unpushed work.

evidence.quote: Two machines, or two agents, on the same vault physically cannot overwrite each other's uncommitted or unpushed work: they're on different branches with different keys.

claims.text: Pushes use compare-and-swap on the server, so a stale push is rejected rather than overwriting.

evidence.quote: Pushes use compare-and-swap on the server (atomic batch writes): if someone pushed before you, your push is rejected cleanly instead of silently clobbering, pull, merge, push again.

claims.text: Merges are genuine three-way merges per file, and sgit resolve --show gives a verdict that separates genuine conflicts from one-sided or identical changes.

evidence.quote: When histories diverge, sgit runs a genuine three-way merge (common ancestor + ours + theirs) per file.

claims.text: The server never sees contents, filenames, commit messages, branch names or keys; it does see the vault id, object sizes, timing and approximate activity volume.

evidence.quote: Traffic analysis of sizes and timing is a real (if narrow) channel, and pretending otherwise would be marketing, not security.

What the server can see: the vault ID, the size of each encrypted object, and request
  timing. Never filenames, contents, or commit messages.

claims.text: Keys are derived from the vault key with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 600,000 iterations, then HKDF-SHA256 for purpose-specific keys; no custom primitives.

evidence.quote:
Crypto: AES-256-GCM, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 600k iterations, HKDF-SHA256. No custom
  primitives; output matches the browser Web Crypto API byte for byte.

claims.text: The site itself says the structure-key split, separating metadata access from content access, is designed but not yet active.

evidence.quote: Today, vault objects are encrypted under the read key, activating the structure-key split across structural objects is an in-progress, reviewed design change

claims.note: A stated limit of the design, worth keeping beside claim c10.

claims.text: A generated vault passphrase carries about 124 bits of entropy, and there is no password reset or recovery.

evidence.quote: A generated passphrase is 24 characters over a 36-symbol alphabet
there is no password reset. If you lose the vault key, nobody, including us, can recover the contents.

claims.text: The CLI and the SG/Vault browser client are independent implementations of one wire format, held together by test vectors.

evidence.quote: The sgit CLI and the SG/Vault browser client are independent implementations of the same encrypted wire format, kept interoperable through a versioned contract with test vectors.

claims.text: A read key is derived one way from the vault key, so it can be published and can never be turned into write access.

evidence.quote: A read key carries read only, and is derived from the vault key by a one-way function, so a read key can never be turned back into write access.

claims.text: Revoking a read key is not retroactive: anyone who fetched the objects keeps them.

evidence.quote: Revocation is not retroactive. Anyone who has fetched the objects keeps them; rotating protects future commits only.

claims.text: Append lanes let a sender write to a vault with no account; the response is blind, and the server stores only hashes of the capabilities and ciphertext.

evidence.quote: The server stores SHA-256 hashes of the first three and checks H(presented) == stored. It never holds a raw capability key, and never holds a private key at all. Compromising the server yields hashes and ciphertext.

claims.text: Deriving the lane address from a public key is proposed, not shipped; today the token is agreed out of band.

evidence.quote:
That derivation is PROPOSED, no shipped command emits it, so today
  you agree the token out of band.

claims.note: The shape diagram on the messaging page draws append_token = H(pubkey); the text marks it as proposed.

claims.text: On a 600-commit, 9,400-file vault a one-folder scoped clone took 14 s against 80 s for a full clone (CLI team's numbers, one sandbox).

evidence.quote: On a shared CRM vault of about 600 commits and 9,400 files

claims.note: Single environment, vendor-measured; the site's own check on a 55-file vault gave 9.7 s against 3.0 s.

claims.text: A partial clone is not an access boundary: the clone holds the vault key and can widen to any folder.

evidence.quote: A partial clone is not an access boundary. --path decides what is downloaded, not what can be read

claims.text: The site states sgit is beta and has no compliance certification.

evidence.quote: sgit is beta; it has no compliance certification of any kind.

claims.text: Commit author attribution is not yet recorded; per-agent identity comes from branch ids, not signed authorship (as stated on the limitations page of v0.7.87).

evidence.quote: Commit author attribution is not yet recorded, in multi-agent vaults, per-agent identity currently comes from branch IDs, not signed authorship.

claims.note: May be stale: llms.txt lists an update to sgit-ai 0.21.0 that mentions signatures; not reconciled here.

evidence.quote: The excess falls from twelve actions to seven to none; the mandated limits that rest on hope stay at six in the first two designs and fall to none in the third.
